title: How does this delay line travel faster than light?
body:
Board design:

Fab: 1.6mm thick substrate, εr ~ 4.8, seems to be normal FR-4 stock. (I actually measure more like ~5.3, but I don't have very good mechanical tolerances in the measurement, and it's only a low-frequency figure.) 0.56mm width trace should be close to 100Ω Z0 (not that fab tolerances are great here, either; but neither does Z0 vary all that quickly). Trace length is 152mm as shown.

Circuit is a dual single-balanced mixer to generate quadrature outputs. There are 1:1+1 baluns (L7-L9, L16-L18; pads provided by some 1210 footprints crudely overlaid as I don't need to make proper footprints or models for this project), BAS70-07 dual diodes (D1, D2), some damping resistance (R8/R15, 470Ω), and a 3rd-order diplexing filter (right half). (Grounds provided by vias, or copper foil wrapped around board edge. Bottom side is 100% contiguous.)

(Balun cores are similar to Fair-Rite 2861002702, and windings are 2t 28AWG each.)

Reference input is at the bottom-middle, by R14. Source is a tuned amplifier, delivering about 10dBm into 50Ω, at 300MHz.

Signal input is at the center-right, by R13. Source is wideband amplifier, in the -10 to 0dBm range. Tone is variable, in this case shifted by a couple MHz relative to ref.

As frequency is fairly high, I opted for a delay line to obtain phase shift. One full cycle of 300MHz is 3.33ns; a quarter is 0.833ns, and at c ~ 56% c0, 140mm should be required. Ideally, this generates quadrature, or a bit past, really (I designed in extra, expecting to cut it down as needed).

Instead I measured 35° between difference I and Q outputs, implying c ~ 156% c0.

Somehow, I doubt I have tachyonic substrate here.

Ok, maybe something goofy is going on. I cut the trace down like so,

which should be closer to 74mm. I measured 13° phase shift. Well, that seems roughly consistent at least, but velocity is still very wrong.

To better clarify board construction (since it is a bit ad-hoc compared to your usual fare), consider this rendition:

Pink: board outline
Purple hash: component body
Via rows along edge: wraparound foil

With measurement for scale:

Overall board is 48 x 26.2 mm.

Schematic:

There is no full schematic. It's a simple enough circuit it's built in PCB mode. Signal path should be easy enough to read off the layout. Just in case, a block diagram:

Sig and Ref are 50Ω sources. I and Q (by L15 and L12 respectively) are terminated into 100Ω (actually 47Ω + terminated BNC).
